headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default; n8n’s server-side execution raises the blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and execute workflow nodes, while Semantic Kernel can use MCP/OpenAPI tools and application-defined files. A shared filesystem or file handoff lets attacker-controlled content from one agent be treated as instructions by the other. This is plausible in default orchestration, though not proven to be automatic.
conditions: IF agent_a writes workflow output to a file that agent_b later reads as prompt content
IF agent_b ingests file contents or MCP payloads without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Add a strict file allowlist for inter-agent handoff
Prefix all handoff files with machine-readable provenance metadata
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from shared folders
requires-engineering: add content-signing or provenance verification

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have read/write filesystem access and broad network egress, so sensitive workflow data touched by n8n can flow into Semantic Kernel outputs or upstream APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, but n8n’s server filesystem and Semantic Kernel’s application-defined files create a realistic leakage path in common deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or datastore
IF either agent forwards file contents to a third-party model or API
mitigations: Store each agent’s files in separate directories
Rotate or scope API keys per agent
Turn off automatic file attachment to model calls
Review outbound integrations for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n can write the server filesystem and run command/code nodes, while Semantic Kernel can also write files and call plugins/MCP tools. If both target the same mutable workspace, concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite each other. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so uncertainty should be treated as higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared datastore
IF either agent mutates shared plugin state without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output paths per agent
Serialize writes through a single queue
Use per-agent credentials and storage namespaces
Add file-locking around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n’s AI Agent node orchestrates tools, and Semantic Kernel is a function-calling/plugin framework; that makes it plausible for one agent’s output to become the other’s input without verification. If n8n-generated facts or tool results are consumed by Semantic Kernel as authoritative, downstream actions can amplify a single error into incorrect API calls or workflow actions.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without a validation step
IF agent_a’s tool results are forwarded into agent_b prompts or plugins
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step
Require structured schemas for inter-agent messages
Log and diff tool outputs before reuse
Block direct action execution from unverified text
requires-engineering: add policy gates for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: n8n handles whatever the workflow processes, while Semantic Kernel touches application context and may send data to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP servers. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch if regulated data is routed through both stacks. The profiles do not specify certifications, so the safest reading is a moderate compliance risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by both agents
IF one agent’s logging or retention exceeds the other’s policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing it
Keep regulated data out of third-party model calls
Align retention settings across both systems
Document residency for each integration
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing
